search_strategy: Cloned curator, read llm.py/db.py/curator_response.py in full first (lines 254-1587). Then queried Gitea issues/PRs and comments (mostly upstream noise, no company record found there). Dumped ALL 228 BookStack wiki pages with comments to /tmp/wiki.txt (this task has NO wiki carriers per the answer key, so this was wasted effort, though it correctly ruled wiki out). Dumped the full Mattermost history of all ~10 channels to a single /tmp/chat.txt (~10k lines). From there the agent did NOT read chronologically channel-by-channel; it ran broad keyword greps ('identity', 'run_hash', 'stamp', 'disable_cache', 'run_id', 'backend_params', etc.), collected the hit line numbers into 'tight.txt'/'hits.txt', then expanded small windows (`sed -n 'N,Mp'`) around clusters of hits and read those in chunks (steps 31-59). This surfaced the majority (30/48) of remarks, all of which cluster tightly around technical keywords the agent searched for. The 18 remarks it missed are disproportionately the colloquial, non-jargon-bearing turns of an exchange ('so basically ya, same thing bit me', 'quick one before i forget', 'while you're in there') that carry the requirement's information but not a keyword the agent's grep list included — the agent never did an exhaustive per-channel, chronological read of any channel (#code-review has 11 remarks but posts run far higher), so any remark sitting in a gap between keyword-hit windows was invisible. #help (1 remark) and #viewer (2 of 313 posts) were essentially never independently searched.

Reward 0.875 reflects one lost fact (g4.r1.scope) out of eight, not an infra or provenance failure.
notable: Only ONE fact was lost (g4.r1.scope), and it was lost for a narrow, specific reason: the copy-on-read half of `LLM.backend_params` was carried by exactly two remarks (g4.r1.fix27, g4.r1.l-params-copy); one was read but never reasoned about, the other never surfaced at all (line 6915-6917 vs line 4715).

The agent's own synthesis Analysis at line 6786 states the backend_params rule almost backwards relative to fix27: it frames backend_params as 'the dict given at construction' (implying a live handle) rather than 'a copy handed out fresh each time' — a case of the agent's stated reasoning contradicting a remark it had already scrolled past 2000+ lines earlier without citing.

All four herrings were correctly not followed — in every case the agent's keyword-grep clusters surfaced the herring and its reversal in the same or an adjacent window (e.g. lines 2649-2662, 3772-3777), so the reversal was read within the same 'Current Terminal Screen' as the herring, leaving little chance to believe the stale decision.

Search strategy was clue-density-driven, not exhaustive: full wiki and full chat were dumped to disk, but only tight-keyword grep clusters were actually read line-by-line. This recovered 30/48 remarks (the technically-worded ones) while missing 18 casually-worded ones scattered across less-frequently-hit channels (#help, #viewer, #random) — none of which mattered for scoring except fix27/l-params-copy.

The task's own answer key notes this task has no wiki or mail carriers; the agent spent roughly a third of its early steps (up to step ~30) dumping and grepping BookStack for nothing, before pivoting to Mattermost where all 48 remarks actually live.
